newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan May M2 money supply up 8.99 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan May M2 money supply up 8.99 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Taiwan's broadest money supply measure, M2, grew 8.99 percent in May from a year earlier, the central bank said on Wednesday.

The year-on-year May M2 increase was the first time the figure fell below the central bank's target zone of 9-14 percent growth since the central bank adopted a new, broader definition of M2 in January.

Analysts have said the new broader definition could be expected to add 1.0 to 1.5 percentage points to the closely watched indicator. Before the shift, it had been 16 months since M2 growth had hit target.
The M2 growth in May was lower than an average forecast of 9.438 percent compiled from a June 23 Reuters poll of Taiwan economists.
M2 growth in April was 9.76 percent year-on-year.
The central bank attributed the low May M2 money supply growth to slowing growth in bank loans and investments and a major rise in government deposits.

The M2 also was slowed by the central bank's unusually high issuance of negotiable certificates of deposit and by a tightening of liquidity at the peak of the state treasury's annual income tax collection, economists said.
National Securities economist Lin Kuo-yang said growth of bank loan approvals continued to be sluggish, reflecting the general slowness of Taiwan's economic recovery.
